text:
bryan-cust: Hey team — since yesterday ~22:00 UTC we're intermittently seeing 403s from the inference API for our service key. Fails around 1 in 8 requests. sample req id: req_7a9f3c2b. No changes on our end.

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a curl repro and the response headers/body? Also which endpoint (host/region)?

bryan-cust: us-west-2, endpoint: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate. curl I'm using (sanitized):

curl -i -X POST
  -H "Authorization: ServiceKey sk_live_XXXXX"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_987"
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

response (one of the failing calls):
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2026 22:14:12 GMT
X-Request-ID: req_7a9f3c2b
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"forbidden","message":"signature verification failed","request_id":"req_7a9f3c2b"}

sam-eng: Thanks — that "signature verification failed" usually means one of: signed header missing/mismatch, clock skew, or wrong org/project header that changes verification scope. Do you include any proxy that might rewrite headers?

bryan-cust: We have an edge proxy (nginx) that adds some headers and strips hop-by-hop ones. We don't intentionally rewrite Authorization or X-Org-ID. We'll confirm.

maria-support: Can you try a direct curl from a laptop (no proxy) and paste the raw response + the exact command you run? Also grab the X-Request-ID from the failing response. We'll fetch server-side logs for that request id.

bryan-cust: Trying now, direct from my laptop, exact command below, getting same error: req_8b2e1d90

curl -i -X POST
  -H "Authorization: ServiceKey sk_live_XXXXX"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_987"
  -d '{"input":"probe"}'
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Request-ID: req_8b2e1d90
{"error":"forbidden","message":"signed header mismatch","request_id":"req_8b2e1d90"}

jen-devex: Noted the different messages: "signature verification failed" vs "signed header mismatch" — both indicate mismatch in what's signed vs what's received. Can you run:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: ServiceKey sk_live_XXXXX"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_987"
  -H "X-Debug-Collect: 1"
  -d '{"input":"probe","meta":{"client_time":"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}}'

That will surface timing and we can correlate logs. If you can, paste the full response headers including any Set-Cookie or intermediary headers.

bryan-cust: Ran with X-Debug-Collect, got: req_8b2e9001. Response includes:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Request-ID: req_8b2e9001
X-Verification-Notes: signed_headers:[authorization,content-type,x-org-id], received_headers:[authorization,content-type]
{"error":"forbidden","message":"missing signed header x-org-id","request_id":"req_8b2e9001"}

sam-eng: Aha — server expected X-Org-ID to be part of the signature (signed_headers) but our gateway didn't see it in received headers list. That matches a proxy stripping/normalizing the header. If NGINX forwards X-Org-ID it must be set with proxy_set_header X-Org-ID $http_x_org_id; otherwise it might be lost.

maria-support: To help us triage, please collect a debug bundle: run the failing request with X-Debug-Collect and then paste the X-Request-ID (you already did). We'll pull server logs and the signing payload for that req id.

ops-bot: syslog: pulled logs for req_8b2e9001 -> signer_payload="POST\n/v1/generate\ncontent-type:application/json\nauthorization:ServiceKey sk_live_XXXXX\n" server_seen_headers=[authorization,content-type]

sam-eng: The signer_payload shows x-org-id absent. We should check if the customer's edge strips headers starting with X- or lowercases them. Our signing is case-insensitive for header names but proxy may have deleted it.

bryan-cust: Confirmed: our nginx config had
proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
# missing proxy_set_header X-Org-ID $http_x_org_id
I added proxy_set_header X-Org-ID $http_x_org_id; and restarted. Trying again...

bryan-cust: After change — direct through proxy now returns 200 OK, req_8b2f3344. Thanks!

maria-support: Awesome — can you confirm no other services rewrite Authorization? Also would be great if you could rotate the service key after verifying to be safe (we logged the key value in internal logs briefly for triage).

sam-eng: We'll close the loop on our side: add a check in docs and a short note in the infra-runbook to warn about proxies dropping X-Org-ID and similar signed headers. Ticket: INF-1224.

jen-devex: I'll follow up with a short KB: "403 signed header mismatch from proxies — repro & fix" and paste the nginx snippet. :white_check_mark:

bryan-cust: Thanks team! Appreciate the fast help.

maria-support: Marking thread for follow-up: ask customer to rotate key, confirm 48h no regressions, then we can close. :thumbsup:
